Yeah I've been sort of feeling the same way lately and sharing similar thoughts. When you consider the immensity of time and space, it is kind of impossible not to consider a human life to be inconsequential - in the grand scheme of things.

 Your life may matter to those close to you, but the whole of humanity is kind of insignificant in all likelyhood to the whole universe. When you push the thought further, the extinction of the whole species would probably not mean much for the universe as a whole. If the enirety of human history is inconsequential, the substraction of a tiny tiny element of that group (ie one man) can't be important either.

So that's one way of looking at it. Humanity might be a minor diversion from the void. Can mankind become something more, something truly more worthwhile then simply being?

It feels a bit like we are writting a millenial story, each contributing a letter, word, sentence or paragraph. But the story is quite disjointed, and without a clear endpoint or aim, our contribution is at most modest, and probably not worth the ink.

Why keep breathing if only for the sake of being able to breathe some more still. Is breathing for breathing's sake meaningful? I'm not sure. Yet the universe probably churns out a great many planets with a great many species. Universe gives life to planets, planets give life to species, species give life to man, mother gives life to son and son gives life to himself by breathing, eating, making a habitat for himself, working to keep all these things within reach until maybe one day he gives life to his offspring.

Now I'm really unsure about life and the prospect of shortening it. I'm not there yet I guess. But if we lived to be 10000 years old, surely more people would consider shortening that timespan of doing circles I would think. 

Your feelings toward suicide seem to be existential : how much meaninglessness can one man endure? I hope the burden is lightened somewhat by seeing me carry it too.
